I read the backend module and the existing canteen front end. Here's where things actually stand before we design anything.

## What's already there

**Backend** (6 controllers): `ItemMaster`, `MealSession`, `MenuPlan`, `MenuPublish`, `MealBooking`, `CanteenDashboard`.

**Front end** (`src/app/module/canteen-management/`): `item-master`, `meal-session`, `menu-plan`, `menu-publish` — all admin screens, all built.

**Missing: the employee side.** And it's already half-wired — `Migration_CanteenMealBooking_20261023.sql` inserted a live `HR_MenuItems` row at `/canteen-management/meal-booking` (DisplayOrder 105, IsActive 1) with VIEW/CREATE/DELETE actions. So that menu entry is in the sidenav today and leads to a dead route. `PermissionsConstants.cs:30` even says so: *"No web screen — the HR_MenuItems row only carries the permission."*

## The real gap is an API, not a layout

A booking screen needs, for each date × session: *is there a menu and what's on it, what do I pay, has ordering closed, did I already book.* Today:

| Need | Available? |
|---|---|
| My bookings in a range | ✅ `GetMyBookings(fromDate, toDate)` |
| My rate per session | ✅ `GetEmployeeMealRates/{employeeMasterId}` (+ `orderCutoffDescription`) |
| **Menu for a given day + session** | ❌ `GetAllMenuPlans` is month-level with `itemNames` concatenated; `GetMenuPlanById` is per-day but returns item *IDs* and needs a plan id |
| **Has the cutoff passed for 26 Oct lunch?** | ❌ computable from `orderCutoffTime` + `orderCutoffDaysBefore`, but only in **the canteen's time zone**, which the browser doesn't know |

That last row matters. `MealOrderCutoff` exists precisely so "the rule shown and the rule enforced cannot drift apart" — if the Angular app does its own cutoff math off the browser clock, we reintroduce the drift, and an employee abroad sees a different deadline than the API enforces. Same for menu: without it, the grid offers every day and the API answers `"No menu that day"` only after they hit Book.

My recommendation: **one new endpoint**, `GET api/MealBooking/GetMealPlanner?fromDate&toDate`, returning per date × active session — `sessionName`, `items[]`, my `employeeShare`/`companyShare`, `orderCutoffDescription`, `isClosed`, `bookingId` (if booked), `canBook`/`canCancel`. One call fills the screen, the server stays the only place the deadline is decided, and the **mobile app gets the same benefit** — it has exactly this problem.

## One API shape issue worth deciding now

`BookMealsRequest` is `{ MSessionIds[], Dates[] }` — a **cartesian product**. If someone ticks Breakfast on Monday and Lunch on Tuesday, the FE can't express that in one call; it would have to send two requests (grouping the selection by identical session-sets), or send a superset and over-book. A free-form grid is the natural UI here, so either we group client-side, or we add `items: [{ mealDate, mSessionId }]` to the request.

## The UI I'd build

**Meal Booking** at `/canteen-management/meal-booking`, standalone component, `canActivateEmployeeOnly` guard (it's a "me as an employee" screen), DevExtreme + the Bootstrap grid idiom the menu-plan form already uses — there's no calendar/scheduler component anywhere in the app, so a hand-built week grid matches precedent.

- Week strip, prev/next, current week by default. Columns = days, rows = active meal sessions.
- Each cell: menu items, ₹ employee share, a toggle. Disabled with the reason inline — *no menu*, *closed at 11:59 PM on 23 Oct*, *already booked*.
- Sticky footer: "Book 5 meals · ₹250" → `BookMeals` → per-meal result summary ("4 booked, 1 already booked").
- Booked cells flip to a Cancel action → `CancelMeals(bookingIds)`.
- A **My Bookings** tab: month history + total employee share, straight from `GetMyBookings`.

Two optional extras, both needing new APIs: a **kitchen headcount** ("how many lunches tomorrow") — note `CanteenDashboardRepository` still counts menu-publish recipients as a proxy and its comment says *"no consumption/order table exists"*, which is stale now that `HR_CMS_MealBooking` is there — and an **admin bookings register** (all employees for a date, exportable).

Four calls to make:

---
name: hrms-two-migration-folders
description: HRMS keeps DB migrations in two unconnected folders; porting SolutionOneWeb work to the backend needs a counterpart script or EF fails with "Invalid column name"
metadata:
  type: project
---

The HRMS workspace has two independent sets of SQL migrations, and they are never synced automatically:

- `HRMS_Payroll/SolutionOneWeb/App_Data/DbMigrations/NNN_*.sql` — numbered, run against the legacy payroll DB by the DbMigrationRunner tool.
- `HRMS_BackEnd/SolutionOne_DataAccessLayer/SqlScripts/Migration_<Thing>_<yyyyMMdd>.sql` — hand-run against the HRMSystem DB that `HrmsystemContext` uses.

**Why:** The CTC Structure / Annexure-I feature was ported from SolutionOneWeb into the .NET backend (commits "Merge niraj_development: the SolutionOneWeb port run"). The entity + context got `CtcSection` → column `CTCSection`, but no backend SqlScripts counterpart to `239_SalaryHeadCtcSection.sql` was written, so on 2026-10-23 *every* `HrSalaryHeadMasters` query — including the unrelated `GetAllSalaryHeadMasters` — died with `Invalid column name 'CTCSection'`. EF selects every mapped column, so one missing column breaks the whole entity, not just the new feature.

**How to apply:** When a SolutionOneWeb port adds or changes a column, check `SqlScripts/` for a matching `Migration_*.sql` before assuming the backend DB has it; if absent, port the numbered script across (keeping the `IF OBJECT_ID / COL_LENGTH ... IS NULL` idempotent guards the folder uses). When an "Invalid column name" error appears from `HrmsystemContext`, grep the column in `HRMS_Payroll/.../DbMigrations` first — the fix is usually a missing backend script, not a code bug. Related: [[hrms-stale-script-numbers-in-comments]].

Noted — mobile-friendly is now a first-class constraint, not a polish pass. That actually changes the week grid design, so let me fold it in.

I checked how the app does responsive: `LayoutService` publishes `app-mobile` / `app-tablet` classes on `<body>` (breakpoints 767.98px / 1023.98px) and CSS owns the rest — but only `sidenav.component.scss` consumes it today. Everything else is Bootstrap `col-md-*` plus media queries. `CommonGridComponent` already has `@media` blocks at 768px and 480px. So: plain media queries in component SCSS, matching precedent, with `:host-context(body.app-mobile)` only where the DOM structure has to change.

## Responsive behaviour of the booking grid

The 5-column grid you picked doesn't survive a 375px screen, so it degrades in two steps:

| Width | Layout |
|---|---|
| ≥992px | Full week grid as previewed — day columns × session rows |
| 768–991px | 3–4 days visible, horizontal scroll with CSS snap, session-name column sticky left |
| <768px | **Stacks by day.** A scrollable day-chip strip (`Mon 27` `Tue 28` …) doubles as navigation and overview — a dot for booked, dimmed for closed. Below it, that day's sessions as full-width cards: name + serving time, menu items, ₹, and the whole card is the tap target |

Mobile specifics I'll build in:
- **Fixed bottom action bar** — "4 meals · ₹110" with a full-width Book button, sitting above `env(safe-area-inset-bottom)`. Thumb reach, always visible, no hunting for a footer.
- **No hover-only information.** "Closed at 11:59 PM on 23 Oct" prints *in* the cell, never a tooltip — a phone has no hover.
- **≥44px touch targets**, whole-card tap rather than a 16px checkbox.
- **No `dx-data-grid` on this screen at all.** It's used for the admin register (which already has mobile CSS) and My Bookings gets a card list under 768px.
- Short date labels on mobile, full on desktop.

## The build, in order

**Backend first** (the FE can't be written against APIs that don't exist):

1. `GET api/MealBooking/GetMealPlanner?fromDate&toDate` — per date × active session: `items[]`, my `employeeShare`/`companyShare`, `orderCutoffDescription`, `isClosed`, `bookingId`, `canBook`/`canCancel`. Server keeps owning the deadline via `MealOrderCutoff`. Serves the mobile app too.
2. `BookMealsRequest.Items[]` — additive `[{ mealDate, mSessionId }]`; `MSessionIds`/`Dates` stay so the mobile app isn't broken, and the service unions both into one set.
3. `GET api/CanteenDashboard/BookingCounts?fromDate&toDate` — real per-session counts from `HR_CMS_MealBooking`, with the Daily/Adhoc split. This also retires the stale comment in `CanteenDashboardRepository` that says *"no consumption/order table exists in the schema"* — it does now.
4. `GET api/MealBooking/GetBookingRegister` — all employees' bookings, filtered and paged, for the admin register.
5. SQL + RBAC: two new `HR_MenuItems` rows (`/canteen-management/booking-register`, `/canteen-management/canteen-dashboard`) and grants, in the idempotent preview→apply shape `Migration_CanteenMealBooking_20261023.sql` already uses, plus the matching `PermissionsConstants` entries.

**Then the front end:**

6. `meal-booking/` — planner (week grid) + My Bookings tab, routed at the existing dead `/canteen-management/meal-booking`, behind `canActivateEmployeeOnly`.
7. `booking-register/` — `CommonGridComponent`, card fallback under 768px.
8. `canteen-dashboard/` — count tiles, 2-up on phone.
9. `Specs/FRONTEND_CHANGES_CANTEEN_MEAL_BOOKING.md`, matching the `FRONTEND_CHANGES_*` convention the repo uses per module.

/*
    Canteen: Meal Booking (mobile app)
    Date   : 2026-10-23

    WHAT IT ADDS
      Part 1 - HR_CMS_MealBooking: one row per employee + meal date + meal session. The price
               (EmployeeShare / CompanyShare) and the Daily/Adhoc type are copied from the employee's
               Meal Plan and the Meal Session when the meal is booked, so a later rate change never
               changes a meal already booked. Cancelling sets Status = 'Cancelled' - rows are never

      it. These two are about everyone's meals - who ate what, and what the whole company is being
      charged. An employee who may book their own lunch must not thereby be able to read the register,
      so they are their own HR_MenuItems rows with their own grants.

      EXPORT is granted on the register alongside VIEW: the canteen office downloads it to reconcile
      with the contractor's bill, and a register nobody can export is a register nobody can use.

      the new rights within 5 minutes - no re-login needed.

             (N'HR_RolesMaster'), (N'HR_RolePermissions')) AS t(n)
WHERE OBJECT_ID(N'dbo.' + t.n, N'U') IS NULL;

IF NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM [dbo].[HR_MenuActions] WHERE [ActionCode] = 'EXPORT')
    INSERT INTO [dbo].[HR_MenuActions] ([ActionCode], [ActionName], [IsActive]) VALUES ('EXPORT', 'Export', 1);

   PART 2 - The two menu rows
   ════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════ */

# Frontend Changes — Task Management Module (new)

Backend is done (API only — no new DB migration needed; every table this module uses
(`HR_TaskMaster`, `HR_TaskComment`, `HR_TaskAttachment`, `HR_TaskTypeMaster`) already exists from the
legacy `hr_payroll` port). No Angular pages exist for this yet — this doc is the contract to build
against.

Four screens, four controllers, one shared workflow:

- **Task Type Master** (`api/TaskType`) — admin-ish master list feeding the mandatory "Task Type"
  field on every task.
- **Task Management** (`api/TaskManagement`) — the *creator's* screen: assign work, review what
  comes back.
- **My Tasks** (`api/MyTasks`) — the *assignee's* screen: accept, work, submit.
- **Task Dashboard** (`api/TaskDashboard`) — read-only KPIs/charts/drill-down over the same data.

## 1. The state machine (Task Management + My Tasks)

```
Assigned --Accept--> Accepted --StartWork--> InProgress --SubmitForReview--> Submitted
                                                  ^                              |
                                                  |                    Approve() |  RequestRework()
                                                  +------- Rework <--------------+
                                                            |
                                                    SubmitForReview()
                                                            v
                                                        Submitted   (loops back)

Approve(Submitted) --> Closed        [terminal - nothing can leave this state]
Cancel(anything except Closed/Cancelled) --> Cancelled  [terminal]
```

Both screens are two faces on the **same backend state machine** (`ITaskService`) — there is no
separate creator-side vs assignee-side business logic, so the two screens' behavior cannot drift
apart. A few rules worth knowing before you build the UI around them:

- **Progress is one of exactly `0, 25, 50, 75, 100`** — not a free slider. Render it as a fixed
  5-step control (buttons or a stepped slider), not a numeric input.
- **A task past its `dueDate` at submit time requires a delay reason.** `SubmitForReview` returns
  `400` with a message naming the due date if `delayReason` is missing on a late submission — show
  that field conditionally (you can pre-check lateness client-side against `dueDate` to decide
  whether to show it before the user even tries to submit, but the server is the actual gate).
- **`RequestRework` requires `remarks`; `Approve` does not.** Different validation on the same
  popup form depending on which button is pressed.
- **Progress cannot be changed while a task is `Submitted`** — the API returns a message

# Frontend Changes — Canteen Meal Booking (new screens)

Date: 24-Oct-2026

Backend is done. One new migration (`Migration_CanteenAdminScreens_20261024.sql`, RBAC rows only —
no tables; `HR_CMS_MealBooking` already exists from `Migration_CanteenMealBooking_20261023.sql`).

Three screens to build. The first one's `HR_MenuItems` row has been live since 23-Oct and currently
leads nowhere, so the sidebar already offers a link that 404s — that is what this fixes.

| Screen | Route | Who |
|---|---|---|
| **Meal Booking** | `/canteen-management/meal-booking` | every employee, for their own meals |
| **Bookings Register** | `/canteen-management/booking-register` | canteen office, everybody's meals |
| **Canteen Dashboard** | `/canteen-management/canteen-dashboard` | canteen office, the kitchen's counts |

The three routes must be added to the front-end's `IMPLEMENTED_ROUTES` or the sidebar will keep
hiding them.

**Meal Booking is a personal screen** — put `canActivateEmployeeOnly` on it. A login with no
employee (the `edp` admin, operator accounts) has no meals and the page would come up empty. The
other two are *not* personal: an HR user with no employee record runs them perfectly well, so they
must **not** carry that guard.

## 1. `GET api/MealBooking/GetMealPlanner?fromDate&toDate`

Permission: `VIEW` on `/canteen-management/meal-booking`.

The whole booking screen in one call. Defaults to the week starting today when the dates are
omitted; at most `MealBooking.MaxRangeDays` (92) days.

```jsonc
{
  "fromDate": "2026-10-27", "toDate": "2026-11-02",
  "today": "2026-10-24",            // the CANTEEN's today, not the browser's
  "isCanteenFacility": true,
  "canteenFacilityType": "Adhoc",   // which rate the shares below came from
  "facilityMessage": null,          // set only when isCanteenFacility is false: the one banner to show
  "sessions": [                     // active sessions, in serving order - the grid's row headings
    { "mSessionId": 1, "sessionName": "Breakfast", "startTime": "07:30", "endTime": "09:30",
      "orderCutoffDescription": "11:59 PM the day before the meal",
      "companyShare": 45, "employeeShare": 15 }
  ],
  "days": [
    { "mealDate": "2026-10-27", "dayLabel": "Mon", "dateLabel": "27 Oct",
      "isToday": false, "isPast": false,
      "bookedCount": 1, "bookableCount": 1,
      "meals": [
        { "mSessionId": 1, "sessionName": "Breakfast",
          "items": ["Poha", "Tea"], "hasMenu": true,
          "isClosed": false, "closesAt": "11:59 PM on 26 Oct 2026",
          "companyShare": 45, "employeeShare": 15,
          "bookingId": null, "isBooked": false,
          "canBook": true, "canCancel": false,
          "status": "Bookable",
          "statusMessage": "Order by 11:59 PM on 26 Oct 2026." }
      ] }
  ]
}
```

**`days[].meals` is always the same length and order as `sessions`**, so a grid can index straight
into it — a day with no menu at all still has a cell per session.

### Build the cell off `status`, nothing else

| `status` | Means | `canBook` | `canCancel` |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Bookable` | free to book now | `true` | `false` |
| `Booked` | already booked | `false` | `true` until the deadline |
| `Closed` | the deadline has passed | `false` | `false` |
| `NoMenu` | nothing cooked that day | `false` | `false` |
| `NotEligible` | there is a menu and time, but no canteen facility | `false` | `false` |

`statusMessage` is a finished sentence, worded the same as the reply `BookMeals` / `CancelMeals`
would give. **Print it — do not build your own.** The whole point of the endpoint is that the screen
and the API cannot disagree about a deadline.

**Do not compute the cutoff in the browser.** Deadlines are evaluated in the canteen's own time
zone; a laptop set to another zone (or just a wrong clock) would grey out the wrong cells. That is
also why `today` is in the payload — use it for "today" highlighting instead of `new Date()`.

Money: `companyShare` / `employeeShare` on a **booked** cell are what that meal actually cost when
it was booked, not today's rate, so a rate change never silently restates an old booking. On an
unbooked cell they are today's rate for this employee's plan.

## 2. `POST api/MealBooking/BookMeals` — new `items[]`

Permission: `CREATE` on `/canteen-management/meal-booking`. **Additive change — the old shape still
works and the mobile app needs no update.**

```jsonc
// NEW - name each meal. Use this from a grid of tick boxes.
{ "items": [ { "mealDate": "2026-10-27", "mSessionId": 1 },
             { "mealDate": "2026-10-28", "mSessionId": 2 } ] }

// OLD - every session on every date. Still the shortest way to say "lunch, all next week".
{ "mSessionIds": [2], "dates": ["2026-10-27", "2026-10-28"] }
```

`items` exists because the old shape is a **cartesian product**: breakfast on Monday plus lunch on
Tuesday could not be expressed without also ordering breakfast on Tuesday. When `items` is present
the other two fields are ignored.

Limits: 31 distinct dates (`MaxDatesPerRequest`) and 200 meals per request.

The reply is one result per meal, in day order, each day in serving order — `Booked`,
`Already booked`, `No menu that day`, `Booking closed` or `Invalid meal session`, each with its own
`message`. **A 200 does not mean everything was booked**; `response.message` reads
`"4 of 6 meal(s) booked."`. Summarise the outcomes rather than showing a bare success toast, and
reload the planner afterwards.

## 3. `GET api/MealBooking/GetBookingRegister`

Permission: `VIEW` on `/canteen-management/booking-register` — its own right, deliberately not
`MealBooking`. Every canteen employee holds `MealBooking`; being able to book your own lunch must
not let you read what the whole company eats.

Query: `fromDate`, `toDate`, `mSessionId`, `employeeMasterId`, `search` (employee code or name),
`status` (`Booked` / `Cancelled`, omit for both), `page` (1-based), `pageSize` (default 50, max 500).

```jsonc
{
  "fromDate": "2026-10-01", "toDate": "2026-10-31",
  "page": 1, "pageSize": 50,
  "totalCount": 318, "bookedCount": 301, "cancelledCount": 17,
  "totalCompanyShare": 13545, "totalEmployeeShare": 4515,   // over BOOKED rows only, WHOLE filtered set
  "rows": [
    { "bookingId": 9001, "mealDate": "2026-10-27", "mSessionId": 2, "sessionName": "Lunch",
      "employeeMasterId": 501, "employeeCode": "E-0501", "employeeName": "Asha Nair",
      "canteenFacilityType": "Daily", "companyShare": 40, "employeeShare": 10,
      "status": "Booked", "bookedOn": "2026-10-26T18:04:00", "cancelledOn": null }
  ]
}
```

The totals cover the **whole filtered set**, not the page — they are the figures the canteen is
billed on, and one page of rows cannot add up to them. Show them in a footer that does not change
as you page. `bookedOn` / `cancelledOn` are in the canteen's default time zone (the register spans
employees, so one zone for the column beats a mix).

## 4. `GET api/CanteenDashboard/BookingCounts?fromDate&toDate`

Permission: `VIEW` on `/canteen-management/canteen-dashboard`. Defaults to the week starting today.

```jsonc
{
  "fromDate": "2026-10-27", "toDate": "2026-11-02", "today": "2026-10-24",
  "days": [
    { "mealDate": "2026-10-27", "dayLabel": "Mon", "dateLabel": "27 Oct", "isToday": false,
      "totalMeals": 142,
      "sessions": [
        { "mSessionId": 2, "sessionName": "Lunch", "totalMeals": 96,
          "dailyCount": 88, "adhocCount": 8,
          "companyShare": 3840, "employeeShare": 960,
          "isFinal": true } ] }
  ],
  "sessionTotals": [ /* same cell shape, summed over the range; isFinal is always false here */ ],
  "totalMeals": 712, "totalCompanyShare": 28480, "totalEmployeeShare": 7120
}
```

`isFinal` is the one worth designing around: the ordering deadline has passed, so that number can
no longer move — it is what the kitchen shops for. A count that is **not** final is still a moving
target and should be shown as provisional.

Cancelled bookings are excluded throughout: nobody eats them and nobody is charged for them.

### Not the same as `GET api/CanteenDashboard/Summary`

`Summary` counts the people a menu was **published** to (`HrCmsMenuPublish.TotalRecipients`) —
reach, not appetite. It predates `HR_CMS_MealBooking` and is left alone so nothing reading it
changes meaning underneath. **For meals, use `BookingCounts`.** Don't put the two on one screen
without labelling which is which; they will not agree and they are not supposed to.

## 5. Run order

1. `Migration_CanteenAdminScreens_20261024.sql` — **edit `@RoleCodes` first** (it defaults to
   `ADMIN` only). It adds the two office menu rows and their grants.
2. Deploy the API.
3. Deploy the front end.

Permissions are cached 5 minutes, so grants land within 5 minutes without a re-login.

# Frontend Changes — Canteen Meal Booking (new screens)

Date: 24-Oct-2026

Backend is done. One new migration (`Migration_CanteenAdminScreens_20261024.sql`, RBAC rows only —
no tables; `HR_CMS_MealBooking` already exists from `Migration_CanteenMealBooking_20261023.sql`).

Three screens to build. The first one's `HR_MenuItems` row has been live since 23-Oct and currently
leads nowhere, so the sidebar already offers a link that 404s — that is what this fixes.

| Screen | Route | Who |
|---|---|---|
| **Meal Booking** | `/canteen-management/meal-booking` | every employee, for their own meals |
| **Bookings Register** | `/canteen-management/booking-register` | canteen office, everybody's meals |
| **Canteen Dashboard** | `/canteen-management/canteen-dashboard` | canteen office, the kitchen's counts |

The three routes must be added to the front-end's `IMPLEMENTED_ROUTES` or the sidebar will keep
hiding them.

**Meal Booking is a personal screen** — put `canActivateEmployeeOnly` on it. A login with no
employee (the `edp` admin, operator accounts) has no meals and the page would come up empty. The
other two are *not* personal: an HR user with no employee record runs them perfectly well, so they
must **not** carry that guard.

## 1. `GET api/MealBooking/GetMealPlanner?fromDate&toDate`

Permission: `VIEW` on `/canteen-management/meal-booking`.

The whole booking screen in one call. Defaults to the week starting today when the dates are
omitted; at most `MealBooking.MaxRangeDays` (92) days.

```jsonc
{
  "fromDate": "2026-10-27", "toDate": "2026-11-02",
  "today": "2026-10-24",            // the CANTEEN's today, not the browser's
  "isCanteenFacility": true,
  "canteenFacilityType": "Adhoc",   // which rate the shares below came from
  "facilityMessage": null,          // set only when isCanteenFacility is false: the one banner to show
  "sessions": [                     // active sessions, in serving order - the grid's row headings
    { "mSessionId": 1, "sessionName": "Breakfast", "startTime": "07:30", "endTime": "09:30",
      "orderCutoffDescription": "11:59 PM the day before the meal",
      "companyShare": 45, "employeeShare": 15 }
  ],
  "days": [
    { "mealDate": "2026-10-27", "dayLabel": "Mon", "dateLabel": "27 Oct",
      "isToday": false, "isPast": false,
      "bookedCount": 1, "bookableCount": 1,
      "meals": [
        { "mSessionId": 1, "sessionName": "Breakfast",
          "items": ["Poha", "Tea"], "hasMenu": true,
          "isClosed": false, "closesAt": "11:59 PM on 26 Oct 2026",
          "companyShare": 45, "employeeShare": 15,
          "bookingId": null, "isBooked": false,
          "canBook": true, "canCancel": false,
          "status": "Bookable",
          "statusMessage": "Order by 11:59 PM on 26 Oct 2026." }
      ] }
  ]
}
```

**`days[].meals` is always the same length and order as `sessions`**, so a grid can index straight
into it — a day with no menu at all still has a cell per session.

### Build the cell off `status`, nothing else

| `status` | Means | `canBook` | `canCancel` |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Bookable` | free to book now | `true` | `false` |
| `Booked` | already booked | `false` | `true` until the deadline |
| `Closed` | the deadline has passed | `false` | `false` |
| `NoMenu` | nothing cooked that day | `false` | `false` |
| `NotEligible` | there is a menu and time, but no canteen facility | `false` | `false` |

`statusMessage` is a finished sentence, worded the same as the reply `BookMeals` / `CancelMeals`
would give. **Print it — do not build your own.** The whole point of the endpoint is that the screen
and the API cannot disagree about a deadline.

**Do not compute the cutoff in the browser.** Deadlines are evaluated in the canteen's own time
zone; a laptop set to another zone (or just a wrong clock) would grey out the wrong cells. That is
also why `today` is in the payload — use it for "today" highlighting instead of `new Date()`.

Money: `companyShare` / `employeeShare` on a **booked** cell are what that meal actually cost when
it was booked, not today's rate, so a rate change never silently restates an old booking. On an
unbooked cell they are today's rate for this employee's plan.

## 2. `POST api/MealBooking/BookMeals` — new `items[]`

Permission: `CREATE` on `/canteen-management/meal-booking`. **Additive change — the old shape still
works and the mobile app needs no update.**

```jsonc
// NEW - name each meal. Use this from a grid of tick boxes.
{ "items": [ { "mealDate": "2026-10-27", "mSessionId": 1 },
             { "mealDate": "2026-10-28", "mSessionId": 2 } ] }

// OLD - every session on every date. Still the shortest way to say "lunch, all next week".
{ "mSessionIds": [2], "dates": ["2026-10-27", "2026-10-28"] }
```

`items` exists because the old shape is a **cartesian product**: breakfast on Monday plus lunch on
Tuesday could not be expressed without also ordering breakfast on Tuesday. When `items` is present
the other two fields are ignored.

Limits: 31 distinct dates (`MaxDatesPerRequest`) and 200 meals per request.

The reply is one result per meal, in day order, each day in serving order — `Booked`,
`Already booked`, `No menu that day`, `Booking closed` or `Invalid meal session`, each with its own
`message`. **A 200 does not mean everything was booked**; `response.message` reads
`"4 of 6 meal(s) booked."`. Summarise the outcomes rather than showing a bare success toast, and
reload the planner afterwards.

## 3. `GET api/MealBooking/GetBookingRegister`

Permission: `VIEW` on `/canteen-management/booking-register` — its own right, deliberately not
`MealBooking`. Every canteen employee holds `MealBooking`; being able to book your own lunch must
not let you read what the whole company eats.

Query: `fromDate`, `toDate`, `mSessionId`, `employeeMasterId`, `search` (employee code or name),
`status` (`Booked` / `Cancelled`, omit for both), `page` (1-based), `pageSize` (default 50, max 500).

```jsonc
{
  "fromDate": "2026-10-01", "toDate": "2026-10-31",
  "page": 1, "pageSize": 50,
  "totalCount": 318, "bookedCount": 301, "cancelledCount": 17,
  "totalCompanyShare": 13545, "totalEmployeeShare": 4515,   // over BOOKED rows only, WHOLE filtered set
  "rows": [
    { "bookingId": 9001, "mealDate": "2026-10-27", "mSessionId": 2, "sessionName": "Lunch",
      "employeeMasterId": 501, "employeeCode": "E-0501", "employeeName": "Asha Nair",
      "canteenFacilityType": "Daily", "companyShare": 40, "employeeShare": 10,
      "status": "Booked", "bookedOn": "2026-10-26T18:04:00", "cancelledOn": null }
  ]
}
```

The totals cover the **whole filtered set**, not the page — they are the figures the canteen is
billed on, and one page of rows cannot add up to them. Show them in a footer that does not change
as you page. `bookedOn` / `cancelledOn` are in the canteen's default time zone (the register spans
employees, so one zone for the column beats a mix).

## 4. `GET api/CanteenDashboard/BookingCounts?fromDate&toDate`

Permission: `VIEW` on `/canteen-management/canteen-dashboard`. Defaults to the week starting today.

```jsonc
{
  "fromDate": "2026-10-27", "toDate": "2026-11-02", "today": "2026-10-24",
  "days": [
    { "mealDate": "2026-10-27", "dayLabel": "Mon", "dateLabel": "27 Oct", "isToday": false,
      "totalMeals": 142,
      "sessions": [
        { "mSessionId": 2, "sessionName": "Lunch", "totalMeals": 96,
          "dailyCount": 88, "adhocCount": 8,
          "companyShare": 3840, "employeeShare": 960,
          "isFinal": true } ] }
  ],
  "sessionTotals": [ /* same cell shape, summed over the range; isFinal is always false here */ ],
  "totalMeals": 712, "totalCompanyShare": 28480, "totalEmployeeShare": 7120
}
```

`isFinal` is the one worth designing around: the ordering deadline has passed, so that number can
no longer move — it is what the kitchen shops for. A count that is **not** final is still a moving
target and should be shown as provisional.

Cancelled bookings are excluded throughout: nobody eats them and nobody is charged for them.

### Not the same as `GET api/CanteenDashboard/Summary`

`Summary` counts the people a menu was **published** to (`HrCmsMenuPublish.TotalRecipients`) —
reach, not appetite. It predates `HR_CMS_MealBooking` and is left alone so nothing reading it
changes meaning underneath. **For meals, use `BookingCounts`.** Don't put the two on one screen
without labelling which is which; they will not agree and they are not supposed to.

## 5. Run order

1. `Migration_CanteenAdminScreens_20261024.sql` — **edit `@RoleCodes` first** (it defaults to
   `ADMIN` only). It adds the two office menu rows and their grants.
2. Deploy the API.
3. Deploy the front end.

Permissions are cached 5 minutes, so grants land within 5 minutes without a re-login.
EOF

/**
 * Every application route that actually resolves to a screen today.
 *
 * WHY THIS EXISTS
 * ---------------
 * HR_MenuItems is a shared catalogue: it is written by menu-sync runs, by the RBAC screens and
 * by the sibling hr_payroll WebForms project, and it long outlives any single front-end build.
 * It currently holds rows pointing at /income-tax/*, /task-management/*, some /fnf/*,
 * /assets-management/* and /accounts/* whose .NET controllers exist but whose Angular modules
 * have not been written yet, plus a /travel-management/travel-config row whose screen actually
 * lives at /admin/hr-config. Rendering the catalogue verbatim puts those in the sidebar as
 * links that navigate to a blank page.
 *
 * So the sidebar renders a menu row only if its route is listed here. A screen becomes visible
 * the moment someone adds its path to this list - which is the same commit that adds the route
 * to the module - and never a moment before.
 *
 * THIS IS NOT AUTHORIZATION. It answers "does this screen exist", not "may this user open it".
 * Rights stay where they were: HR_UserMenuRights decides which rows reach the browser at all,
 * and AuthService.hasRouteAccess still gates navigation off the unfiltered menu list. A path
 * listed here that the user has no rights to never reaches this check, because it is not in
 * their menus.
 *
 * Keep the entries lower-case, leading-slash, no trailing slash - normalizeRoute() below is
 * what menu rows are put through before they are looked up, and it strips query strings and
 * trailing slashes so "/recruitment/offerlettertemplate/" matches.
 */

content.text:
Both phases are done. Here's what landed.

## Backend

**New endpoints**

| Endpoint | Permission |
|---|---|
| `GET api/MealBooking/GetMealPlanner?fromDate&toDate` | `VIEW` on `/canteen-management/meal-booking` |
| `GET api/MealBooking/GetBookingRegister` | `VIEW` on `/canteen-management/booking-register` *(new)* |
| `GET api/CanteenDashboard/BookingCounts?fromDate&toDate` | `VIEW` on `/canteen-management/canteen-dashboard` *(new)* |

`BookMealsRequest` gained `items: [{ mealDate, mSessionId }]` — additive, the old `mSessionIds × dates` cartesian still works untouched, so the mobile app needs no change. Capped at 200 meals per request alongside the existing 31-date cap.

The two office screens got their own permission modules deliberately: every canteen employee holds `MealBooking`, and booking your own lunch must not let you read what the whole company eats.

`MealOrderCutoff` stays the only place a deadline is decided — the planner's `canBook` / `canCancel` / `statusMessage` come from the same code path `BookMealsAsync` refuses on, and `CanteenDashboardService` computes `isFinal` through it too.

I also corrected the stale `CanteenDashboardRepository` / `CanteenDashboardSummaryModel` comments claiming "no consumption/order table exists" — but I left `Summary` itself computing menu-publish reach as before, rather than silently changing what an existing endpoint means. `BookingCounts` is the real count; the spec says not to put them on one screen unlabelled.

**9 tests added** to `MealBookingServiceTests` — `items[]` booking exactly the named meals and not the rectangle around them, `items` winning over both shapes, and five planner tests including one that asserts the planner closes a meal at the same minute `BookMeals` refuses it.

**`Migration_CanteenAdminScreens_20261024.sql`** — RBAC rows only, no tables. **Edit `@RoleCodes` before running**; it defaults to `ADMIN` only.

## Front end

Three screens, all standalone, matching the existing DevExtreme + Bootstrap-grid idiom. `/canteen-management/meal-booking` was a live `HR_MenuItems` row pointing at nothing since 23-Oct — that dead link now resolves. All three added to `IMPLEMENTED_ROUTES`.

**Mobile-first, as asked:**
- The week grid and the phone's day stack are **two layouts over one `<app-meal-cell>`**, so they can't disagree about price or availability. Grid from 768px (matching `LayoutService`'s own breakpoint); below that, a scroll-snapping day-chip strip with a booked-dot, then that day's meals as full-width cards.
- Between 768–1100px the grid scrolls sideways with the meal-name column stuck left.
- Action bar is `position: fixed` under 768px with `env(safe-area-inset-bottom)` padding, and the page reserves clearance so the last card is never trapped under it.
- Every touch target ≥44px, whole card tappable. **No hover-only information** — the "closed at 11:59 PM on 23 Oct" reason is printed in the cell on phones and kept for screen readers in the grid.
- Booked vs. picked vs. dropping each carry their own icon, not just a colour.
- The register and dashboard inherit `CommonGridComponent`'s mobile detail view / a horizontally-scrolling matrix with a pinned row header; dashboard tiles use `auto-fit` so they go 2-up on a phone with no breakpoint arithmetic.

One tap does two things by context: a free meal gets ticked to book, a booked one ticked to drop. The action bar shows both counts and commits them separately. Booking results are summarised honestly — a 200 that books 4 of 6 says so and names the refusals, rather than showing a bare success toast.

## Two things to flag

**The register truncates at 500 rows per call** and says so in an alert strip when it does. For a company of any size a month's bookings exceed that, so the screen defaults to a single day. If the office needs month-at-a-time export, that wants real server paging or a report export — say the word and I'll add it.

**Nothing was built or run.** No `dotnet build`, no `ng build`, no `dotnet test` — per your setup those are yours. So the 9 new tests are unexecuted, and the C#/Angular here is reviewed but not compiler-checked. The likeliest spots for a first-build complaint are the `[FromQuery] BookingRegisterQuery` binding with its `DateOnly?` members, and the `[style.--mb-day-count]` custom-property binding (the CSS has a `var(--mb-day-count, 7)` fallback either way).

Full API contract for the mobile team is in `HRMS_BackEnd/Specs/FRONTEND_CHANGES_CANTEEN_MEAL_BOOKING.md`.

tools.description:
Launch a new agent to handle complex, multi-step tasks. Each agent type has specific capabilities and tools available to it.

Available agent types are listed in <system-reminder> messages in the conversation.

When using the Agent tool, specify a subagent_type to select an agent: `"fork"` forks yourself (the fork inherits your full conversation context and always runs on your model — a `model` override is ignored); any other type — or omitting it — starts a fresh agent (general-purpose by default).

## When to use

A fresh agent costs more than it looks. It knows only what you put in the prompt, and you see only the summary it sends back — both handoffs drop detail, and neither of you can tell what the other missed. You can't watch it work, only wait or cancel. Its mistakes come back in the same confident register as its findings, and an agent handed your hypothesis tends to return it confirmed. Several at once spend tokens in a burst the user didn't ask for. Weigh those tokens against the accuracy they buy: the user pays for agents you did not need, and pays again for work you redo because you skipped one.

Reach for this when you have independent work to run in parallel, when the user asks for a side quest that shouldn't block your main thread, or when answering would mean reading across several files — delegate that and you keep the conclusion, not the file dumps.

Do the work yourself when it is a handful of tool calls or a lookup whose target you already know; don't delegate a check you could run inline. Delegate review only when you want a read that isn't anchored on yours — then give it the code, not your conclusion. Once you've delegated something, don't also run it yourself; wait for the result. When in doubt, don't spawn.

When you do spawn one, brief it like the peer it is: state the goal and what you have already ruled out, point it at the files and docs worth reading instead of retyping them, and keep the scope explicit and narrow. That brief is the only context it will have, so it is your first lever on every cost above — and if you cannot write a clear one, you do not understand the task well enough to hand it off.

A fork runs in the background and keeps its tool output out of your context. If you are the fork, execute directly — don't re-delegate. Subagents run in the background; you'll be notified when one completes. Never fabricate or predict a pending agent's results — the notification is never something you write yourself; if the user asks before it arrives, say it's still running.

- The agent's final report is not shown to the user — relay what matters.
- Use SendMessage with the agent's ID or name to continue a previously spawned agent with its context intact; a new Agent call starts fresh (except subagent_type: "fork", which inherits your context).
- Each agent type's model, reasoning effort, and tools come from its definition (`.claude/agents/*.md` frontmatter or SDK `agents`).
- `isolation: "worktree"` gives the agent its own git worktree (auto-cleaned if unchanged).

model.description: Optional model override for this agent. Takes precedence over the agent definition's model frontmatter and the configured default subagent model. If omitted, uses the agent definition's model, else the default (inherits from the parent unless a default subagent model is configured). Ignored for subagent_type: "fork" — forks always inherit the parent model.
